content: GROK STACK-WRITE HALLUCINATION — ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (verified from code 2026-05-25). The gap is xAI-side, NOT ours. Evidence: the Grok Ring 2 write path is correct end-to-end (grok_bridge/mcp_filtered.py:100-170 -> bridge_core/interceptor.py intercept() -> pending_writes.py create_pending_write() -> audit.py append_audit_event()); the OpenAI bridge uses the SAME bridge_core pipeline and successfully creates proposals; Ring classification + Ring 2 schema registration are identical across substrates. xAI's Custom Connector dispatches Ring 1 (read) tools to our SSE handler but never dispatches Ring 2 (write-class) tool calls — Grok's runtime turns the tool-call intent into narrated TEXT, not an MCP transport invocation. CONSEQUENCE: the membrane is blind BY DESIGN to a dispatch that never arrives (the audit log only records arriving calls), so any bridge-side post-response probe is moot — nothing arrived to probe. THE REFRAME (load-bearing for all future connectors): a model's narrated write-claim is never evidence; the only trustworthy proof of a Ring 2 write is a bridge-issued, queryable artifact — a real proposal_id present in pending_writes with a valid recomputed audit hash. Built the READ-only proof-of-write primitive (bridge_core.verify_proposal / get_proposal_by_id; found=False is the canonical 'never landed' signal) on branch feat/grok-connector-integrity, additive + hermetically tested (34/34), no live path touched yet. Held for Anthony: Ring 1 exposure of verify_proposal, and a connect-time capability probe (sentinel Ring 2 tool with a 5s arrival Future) that gates RING_2_ENABLED off whenever a connector fails to dispatch writes — that probe would have caught this at handshake. We CANNOT force xAI to dispatch writes; the honest fix is detect-and-refuse-to-trust, not coercion. Same rules must be baked into the Gemini connector from day one.
